content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published an operational handbook titled Module 5: Management of Tuberculosis in Children and Adolescents. This handbook provides comprehensive guidance on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of tuberculosis (TB) in children and adolescents, with a focus on both drug-susceptible and drug-resistant TB. It is available in both electronic and print formats, with ISBNs 978-92-4-004683-2 and 978-92-4-004684-9, respectively. The publication is copyrighted by WHO in 2022, and its content can be adapted and redistributed for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is not permitted, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. The handbook emphasizes that WHO does not endorse any specific organizations, products, or services mentioned within the publication. If the work is translated, a disclaimer must be included, stating that WHO is not responsible for the accuracy or content of the translation, and the original English version remains the authoritative edition. The handbook includes detailed chapters on various aspects of TB management, such as screening children and adolescents living with HIV, TB infection prevention and control, diagnostic approaches for drug-resistant TB, and the management of post-TB health. It also provides practical guidance on managing TB in special situations, such as malnutrition or health emergencies, and offers treatment decision algorithms and dosing guidelines for second-line multidrug-resistant TB regimens. The publication acknowledges the contributions of numerous experts and organizations involved in its development. These include members of the WHO Global TB Programme, external reviewers, and contributors from various institutions worldwide. The handbook also incorporates examples of country experiences with implementing TB care models, including decentralized, family-centered, and integrated approaches to TB services for children and adolescents. The handbook defines key terms and concepts used throughout the text, such as active TB case-finding, contact investigation, and family-centered care. It also provides definitions for age groups, including infants (under 1 year), children (under 10 years), and adolescents (10–19 years). Additionally, it outlines the criteria for advanced HIV disease and extensive pulmonary TB disease, as well as the classification of drug-resistant TB, including extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB). The WHO operational handbook is designed to support healthcare providers, policymakers, and program managers in improving TB care for children and adolescents.
